comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluations find claims C5, C33, C34, C42, C91, C92 about DNA hypomethylation-induced L1TD1 expression to be well-supported. OpenEval cites MethyLight, qRT-PCR, and Western blot data; peer reviewers describe this as a key observation with no methodological concerns.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations support claim C35 regarding parallel regulation of L1TD1 and L1 ORF1p by DNA methylation. OpenEval references Figure 1 supplement data; peer reviewers accept this as expected context showing both the domesticated gene and ancestral element are methylation-regulated.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations strongly support claims C67, C68, C9, C78 about RNA-independent L1TD1-ORF1p interaction. OpenEval cites co-IP and RNase treatment data; peer reviewers describe the evidence as 'solid' and 'compelling' with no concerns about methodology.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations support claims C30, C31, C32 about transcriptome changes in DNMT1 KO cells and compensatory upregulation of de novo methyltransferases. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Significant disagreement. OpenEval finds claims C38-C41, C43, C7, C96 about increased apoptosis/DNA damage well-supported by viability assays and flow cytometry. However, peer reviewers rate this as UNCERTAIN, finding the results 'unexpected' and 'curious' given decreased retrotransposition, questioning whether selection bias confounds the viability data.

Agreement with caveats. Both evaluations support claims C70, C71, C10, C72, C73, C102 about decreased retrotransposition in DKO cells. OpenEval finds the data well-supported; peer reviewers accept the data but note it is 'unexpected' given phenotypic observations, though they do not challenge the data itself.

Strong agreement. Both evaluations support claims C61-C64 about the disconnect between L1TD1-associated transcripts and differentially expressed transcripts. OpenEval cites RNA-seq and RIP-seq comparison; peer reviewers affirm this interpretation of post-transcriptional rather than transcriptional regulation.

Agreement on overlapping claims. Both evaluations support claims C36, C37 about cytosolic localization of L1TD1. OpenEval references immunofluorescence data; peer reviewers accept localization findings as consistent with the functional interaction model. Peer R10 also covers C69 (co-localization with ORF1p).

Agreement on overlapping claims. Both evaluations support claims C52, C86, C87 about L1TD1 affinity for transposon-derived sequences beyond L1. OpenEval cites RIP-seq and TEtranscript analysis; peer reviewers accept these findings without methodological concerns. Peer R9 also covers C65, C66 about AluY upregulation.

Agreement on overlapping claims. Both evaluations support claims C8, C51 about L1TD1 association with L1 transcripts. OpenEval finds RIP-seq data well-supported with appropriate controls; peer reviewers describe the evidence as 'solid' and 'compelling.' OpenEval R4 covers additional claims (C44-C46, C48) not in peer R2.

Partial agreement. Both evaluations support L1TD1-RNA associations (C44, C45, C46, C48 overlap). OpenEval emphasizes RIP-seq methodology and controls; peer reviewers accept the molecular characterization. Peer R6 additionally covers claims about overlap with hESC data (C47, C49, C50, C80) not in OpenEval R4.

Agreement on overlapping claims. Both evaluations support claims C57-C60 about post-transcriptional regulation of L1 ORF1p. OpenEval cites mass spectrometry and qRT-PCR showing no transcript changes; peer reviewers affirm the interpretation that L1TD1 function is 'not modulated at the translational level.' Peer R7 also covers C53, C54, C82, C83.

Agreement on overlapping claims. Both evaluations support claims C53, C54, C82 about proteomic changes in DKO cells. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate statistical methods; peer reviewers accept the disconnect between transcript and protein abundance as supporting post-transcriptional regulation.

Agreement on overlapping claims. Both evaluations support claims C55, C56, C83 about lack of overlap between RIP-seq targets and differentially expressed proteins. OpenEval notes this negative result is important for understanding mechanism; peer reviewers affirm this supports post-transcriptional rather than transcriptional regulation.

Agreement on overlapping claims. Both evaluations support claims C65, C66 about AluY element upregulation upon L1TD1 loss. OpenEval cites TEtranscript analysis; peer reviewers accept these findings as consistent with the overall transposable element interaction model.

Agreement on overlapping claims. Both evaluations support claim C69 about partial co-localization of L1TD1 and ORF1p. OpenEval cites immunofluorescence data; peer reviewers accept this as consistent with co-IP results showing physical interaction.

Disagreement on interpretation. OpenEval rates claim C97 (contradictory observations of increased stress but decreased retrotransposition) as SUPPORTED, accurately describing the observations. Peer reviewers rate this as UNCERTAIN, finding it 'unexpected' and suggesting alternative explanations like selection bias affecting colony counts.

Agreement on overlapping claims. Both evaluations support claims C49, C50 about Gene Ontology enrichment including KRAB domain proteins. OpenEval cites GO analysis; peer reviewers accept the molecular characterization. Peer R6 covers additional RIP-seq claims not in OpenEval R5.

Agreement on overlapping claims. Both evaluations support claim C80 about overlap with hESC study findings. OpenEval notes conserved RNA-binding specificity; peer reviewers accept this as part of the molecular characterization showing L1TD1 function.

Agreement on overlapping claims. Both evaluations support claim C47 citing prior literature (Tahmasebi et al., 2016). OpenEval explicitly validates the citation; peer reviewers accept this as context for the current work.

Partial disagreement. OpenEval supports claim C74 about L1 ORF1p increase in DKO cells as part of well-supported findings. Peer reviewers find this observation 'unexpected' when combined with decreased retrotransposition (C97), rating it as UNCERTAIN and questioning the interpretation.

OpenEval supports claims C1, C11, C12, C76, C77 about L1TD1 structure and evolutionary origin based on established literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/contextual claims.

OpenEval rates claims C79, C98 as UNCERTAIN, noting they are explicitly speculative hypotheses about L1TD1's structural features and effects lacking direct experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval supports claims C2-C4, C16-C29, C99-C101 about L1TD1 expression patterns, developmental/cancer function, and epigenetic regulation based on appropriate literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature-based background claims.

OpenEval supports claims C13-C15, C89, C90 about L1 biology based on established literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims about retrotransposon biology.

OpenEval supports claims C93-C95 about HAP1 cell viability, colorectal carcinoma phenotype, and compensatory mechanisms, noting some speculation is reasonable. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific mechanistic interpretations.
OpenEval rates claim C103 as UNCERTAIN, noting it is speculative about L1TD1's broader biological significance without direct experimental support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval supports claims C104-C106 about the HAP1 cell line model based on citations and methods, though notes validation could be more thorough. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological claims.

OpenEval supports claim C88 as a reasonable evolutionary inference based on RIP-seq data showing L1TD1 association with transposon transcripts. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this evolutionary interpretation.
